items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: I traveled with an all-black rhythm section in the 50s, from Canada. A wonderful pianist called Wray Downes; Archie Alleyne, a drummer; and Bill Britto, a bass player.

ctx.x: Yeah, there was some of that, historically I guess.

Yeah. I never experienced it. I’ve always had wonderful reception and encouragement from musicians. I traveled with an all-black rhythm section in the 50s, from Canada. A wonderful pianist called Wray Downes; Archie Alleyne, a drummer; and Bill Britto, a bass player. I used to stay in black hotels in Detroit and Chicago, to be with them. I didn’t want to be apart and make them feel uncomfortable. But it was prejudiced, there was definite prejudice in those days. It wasn’t easy for any of the black people, was it?
No. But in Toronto, or where you lived, when the black musicians came up there was it, did they have issues?
